title: Designing a notification system

facts.text: A notification service consumes events from a message queue, such as Kafka, and forwards each request to Firebase Cloud Messaging or Apple Push Notification service according to the device platform (Android, iOS, web).
A messaging solution such as FCM is cross-platform, composes, sends, queues and routes notifications reliably, and provides a unified API between app servers and client apps.
When the client app first starts it sends credentials (Sender ID, API Key, App ID) to FCM, which generates a registration token, also called the Instance ID, that must be included in notifications.
The client sends the registration token to the app server, which caches it. Tokens pile up, so the recommended practice is to store each with a timestamp and remove stale ones from time to time.

In the IETF Web Push protocol the user agent POSTs to the push service to subscribe; a 201 response returns the subscription URI and a push resource URI, which must be shared with the application server confidentially.
The application server requests delivery by POSTing the message to the push resource. A 201 response means the push service accepted it, not that it reached the device.

The push service stores messages for intermittently connected devices, which improves delivery reliability. The sender must give a TTL in seconds; once it elapses the service MUST NOT deliver, and the service may retain a message for less time.

A message can carry an urgency of very-low, low, normal or high, defaulting to normal; the device may ask to receive only messages at or above a level, which saves battery because radio use is costly.
A message with a topic of at most 32 characters replaces any outstanding message with the same topic, so a device that was offline gets only the latest update, not outdated or redundant ones.

The device acknowledges a message by an HTTP DELETE; without an acknowledgement the service SHOULD retry until the advertised expiration. Delivery receipts (202 on acceptance, then 204 once acknowledged, or 410 Gone on failure) tell the sender the outcome.

Receipts matter for critical messages: knowing a message arrived avoids retransmission, polling and state resynchronization, while transient messages such as an incoming call, or quickly superseded ones, may not need reliability.
A push service may expire a subscription at any time and MUST answer 404 Not Found to a sender using an expired one, so servers and clients must be prepared to manage changes in subscription state.
Apple's HTTP/2 provider API for APNs allows payloads up to 4 kilobytes and uses TCP port 443, or port 2197 when firewalls block outbound 443.
SMS is a further channel, carried over SMS gateways through an SMSC, with messages of up to 160 characters; businesses such as banks and e-commerce send application-to-person messages this way.
SMS delivery is not guaranteed and senders often cannot tell whether a message arrived in time; studies show about 1% to 5% of messages are lost even in normal operation.

A push service must hold very many open TCP connections and can redistribute load with 307 redirects. Stored messages take significant storage, so it may reject large bodies with 413 but MUST accept bodies of 4096 bytes or less.

notes: thin: the chapter's sources give no functional requirements, scale or estimates, data model, deduplication on the sender side, rate limiting, user preferences or opt-out, or email channel; the typical push-notification architecture (gateway, templates, channel preferences, routers) is the entry Notification system architecture in real-time-communication.

definition.text: A cross-platform Google messaging service that composes, sends, queues and routes push notifications between app servers and client apps.

facts.text: FCM superseded Google Cloud Messaging, adding delivery of push notifications to iOS and web devices as well as Android, behind a unified API between senders and client apps.
On first start the client app sends its credentials to FCM, which generates a registration token (the Instance ID) for that app instance; the token must be included in notifications.
The client passes the token to the app server, which caches it. Storing each token with a timestamp and pruning stale ones keeps the set manageable.
Messages are composed in the console or sent from the app server using the Firebase Admin SDK or HTTP.
FCM queues messages in storage when the device is offline, forwards them to a platform-level transport that handles platform-specific configuration, and routes them to the target devices.
In a typical design a notification service reads events from a message queue or broker such as Kafka and dispatches requests to FCM or APNs, which deliver to user devices.

definition.text: Apple's platform notification service that lets third-party application developers send notification data to applications installed on Apple devices.

facts.text: A notification can carry badges, sounds or custom text alerts.
Apple stated at launch that push notifications conserve battery better than the background processes that pull technology needs to receive notifications.

Apple released an HTTP/2 provider API in December 2015 that replaced the legacy binary interface, shut down at the end of March 2021; its maximum payload is 4 kilobytes, up from 2 kilobytes on the binary interface.
The HTTP/2 provider uses TCP port 443, and port 2197 is allowed when firewalls block outbound access to 443.

definition.text: A mostly paid text messaging service of telephone and mobile systems that lets phones exchange short text messages over cellular networks.

facts.text: Messages carry up to 160 characters. The signaling protocol limits the payload to 140 bytes, and messages can use the default GSM 7-bit alphabet, an 8-bit data alphabet or 16-bit UCS-2 or UTF-16.
SMS gateways let computers send messages over the Internet through a short message service center (SMSC), reaching computers, fixed landlines and satellite phones.
Application-to-person (A2P) SMS goes from an application to a subscriber or back, and businesses such as banks, e-gaming, logistics and e-commerce use it to message customers.
Delivery is not guaranteed, and many implementations give the sender no way to learn whether a message arrived in time.
Messages are treated as lower-priority traffic than voice, and studies show around 1% to 5% are lost entirely even in normal operation, while others arrive long after they matter.
SMS messages are not encrypted, so carriers and third parties can read them, phone-number metadata may leak, and senders can be spoofed.
